faq.question: What does JSON escaping do?
faq.answer: JSON escaping adds backslash characters before special characters (quotes, backslashes, newlines, tabs) so they can be safely included inside a JSON string without breaking the structure.

faq.question: What does JSON unescaping do?
faq.answer: JSON unescaping removes the backslash escape characters, converting escaped sequences like \" and \n back into their original characters (quotes and newlines). Use this when you have an escaped JSON string and need to read the actual content.

faq.question: When should I escape JSON?
faq.answer: Escape JSON when embedding a JSON string inside another JSON document, when including JSON in JavaScript code, when writing JSON to log files, or when pasting JSON into configuration files that require escaped strings.

faq.question: When should I unescape JSON?
faq.answer: Unescape JSON when you receive escaped JSON strings from API responses, webhook payloads, log files, or error messages and need to see the actual JSON content for debugging or further processing.

faq.question: What special characters are escaped in JSON?
faq.answer: The characters that must be escaped in JSON strings are: double quotes ("), backslashes (\), newlines (\n), tabs (\t), carriage returns (\r), backspace (\b), form feed (\f), and any character using the \uXXXX Unicode escape.

faq.question: What is the difference between JSON escaping and HTML encoding?
faq.answer: JSON escaping uses backslashes (\") to handle special characters inside JSON strings. HTML encoding uses ampersands (&quot;) to handle special characters in HTML. They serve the same purpose — preventing syntax conflicts — but use different escape characters and are not interchangeable.

faq.question: Can I escape an entire JSON object, not just a string?
faq.answer: Yes. When you paste a JSON object like {"key": "value"}, the Escape function converts all quotes and special characters so the entire object can be safely embedded as a string inside another JSON document or JavaScript code.

faq.question: Why does my escaped JSON have too many backslashes?
faq.answer: This usually means the input was already escaped before you ran the Escape function — a problem called double escaping. Use the Unescape button to remove the extra backslashes, then check your input before escaping again.

faq.question: How do I handle Unicode characters in JSON strings?
faq.answer: Unicode characters (like é, ñ, 中文, emoji) can appear directly in JSON strings without escaping. However, if you need to escape them, use the \uXXXX format with the 4-digit hex code. For example, é becomes \u00e9.

faq.question: Does this tool work with JSON Lines (JSONL) format?
faq.answer: Yes, you can paste multi-line JSONL content and escape or unescape it. Each line will be processed with the same escaping rules. This is useful for preparing JSONL log data or batch processing.

faq.question: Is there a size limit for the JSON I can escape?
faq.answer: There is no artificial size limit. The tool runs entirely in your browser, so performance depends on your device. For most use cases (up to several MB), it works instantly. Very large files (100MB+) may slow down your browser.

article.title: How to Escape & Unescape JSON Strings Online — Complete Guide
article.content:
What is JSON Escaping?

JSON escaping is the process of adding backslash characters (\) before special characters in a string so it can be safely included inside a JSON document. Special characters like double quotes, backslashes, newlines, and tabs have special meaning in JSON — if you include them raw, the JSON becomes invalid. Escaping tells the parser to treat the character as literal text, not as syntax.

For example, the string She said "hello" contains double quotes that would break a JSON string. After escaping, it becomes She said \"hello\" — valid and safe to embed.

Common Escaped Characters in JSON

JSON defines a small set of characters that must be escaped when they appear inside a string value:

  • \" — Double quote (required, since quotes delimit strings)
  • \\ — Backslash (required, since it introduces escape sequences)
  • \n — Newline / line feed
  • \t — Tab / horizontal tab
  • \r — Carriage return
  • \uXXXX — Unicode character (4-digit hex code)

All other characters can appear directly in a JSON string without escaping, including most emoji and non-ASCII letters.

Real-World Scenarios for JSON Escaping

Escaping JSON for Log Files

When your application writes JSON data to log files (CloudWatch, ELK, Datadog), the log entries themselves are often JSON. If the payload contains nested JSON strings, those inner strings must be escaped. For example, an API request body logged as a string inside a JSON log entry needs proper escaping to keep the log file parseable. Without escaping, your log aggregator will fail to index the entry or split it incorrectly.

Embedding JSON in JavaScript Code

If you need to embed a JSON object inside a JavaScript string (for example, in a test fixture, a config template, or an inline script), you must escape all quotes and backslashes. A common mistake is copying raw JSON into a JS string literal without escaping — this produces a syntax error. Use our JSON escape tool to convert the raw JSON into a valid JavaScript string in one click.

Handling Escaped JSON from Webhooks and APIs

Many APIs return JSON responses where some fields contain escaped JSON strings. For example, a webhook payload might include a payload field whose value is a JSON object encoded as a string. To read the actual data, you need to unescape that string first. This is common with Stripe webhooks, Slack API responses, and event-driven architectures where JSON is passed as a string inside another JSON document.

Working with JSON in Configuration Files

Configuration files (package.json, tsconfig.json, .eslintrc) are JSON, but they sometimes contain string values that include special characters — file paths with backslashes on Windows, regex patterns, or multi-line descriptions. Proper escaping ensures these config files remain valid JSON and can be parsed by tools without errors.

Common Mistakes When Escaping JSON

Double Escaping

The most common mistake is escaping an already-escaped string. For example, if you escape She said \"hello\" a second time, you get She said \\\"hello\\\" — now the backslashes themselves are escaped, producing incorrect output. If your output has more backslashes than expected, you likely double-escaped. Use the Unescape button to revert, then escape only once.

Forgetting to Escape Backslashes

Backslashes must be escaped first, before any other character. If you have a Windows file path like C:\Users\test, it must become C:\\Users\\test in JSON. A common error is escaping quotes but forgetting backslashes, which produces broken JSON that looks almost correct.

Using Wrong Escape Sequences

JSON only supports a limited set of escape sequences: \", \\, \/, \n, \r, \t, \b, \f, and \uXXXX. Sequences like \a, \v, or \0 are invalid in JSON (though valid in some programming languages). Using invalid sequences will cause JSON.parse to throw an error.

Mixing Escaped and Unescaped Content

If you paste a string that is partially escaped (some quotes are escaped, others are not), the escape or unescape operation will produce inconsistent results. Before processing, check whether your input is fully escaped or fully unescaped, and apply the matching operation.

How to Use Our JSON Escape Tool

  1. Paste your JSON string or text into the input field (or upload a file / load from URL)
  2. Click Escape to add escape characters, or Click Unescape to remove them
  3. Copy the result or download it as a file
  4. Use Swap to move the output back to input for reverse operations

All processing happens in your browser — your data is never sent to any server.

faq.question: 哪些特殊字符需要转义？

faq.question: JSON 转义和 HTML 编码有什么区别？

article.title: 如何在线转义和反转义 JSON 字符串 — 完整指南
article.content:
什么是 JSON 转义？

JSON 转义是在字符串中的特殊字符前添加反斜杠（\），使其可以安全地包含在 JSON 文档中。双引号、反斜杠、换行符和制表符在 JSON 中有特殊含义 — 直接使用会破坏 JSON 结构。转义告诉解析器「把这个字符当作普通文本，不要当作语法」。

例如，字符串 She said "hello" 包含会破坏 JSON 的双引号。转义后变成 She said \"hello\" — 合法且可安全嵌入。

JSON 中的常见转义字符

JSON 定义了一组在字符串值中必须转义的字符：

  • \" — 双引号（必须，因为引号是字符串的定界符）
  • \\ — 反斜杠（必须，因为它是转义序列的前缀）
  • \n — 换行符
  • \t — 制表符
  • \r — 回车符
  • \uXXXX — Unicode 字符（4 位十六进制编码）

其他字符（包括大部分 emoji 和非 ASCII 字符）可以直接出现在 JSON 字符串中，不需要转义。

JSON 转义的真实使用场景

日志文件中的 JSON 转义

当应用将 JSON 数据写入日志文件（CloudWatch、ELK、Datadog）时，日志条目本身通常也是 JSON。如果请求体包含嵌套的 JSON 字符串，内部字符串必须转义。例如，作为字符串记录在 JSON 日志中的 API 请求体需要正确转义，否则日志聚合器无法正确索引或拆分条目。

在 JavaScript 代码中嵌入 JSON

如果需要在 JavaScript 字符串中嵌入 JSON 对象（比如测试数据、配置模板或内联脚本），必须转义所有引号和反斜杠。常见错误是把原始 JSON 直接复制到 JS 字符串中而不转义 — 这会产生语法错误。使用我们的 JSON 转义工具一键将原始 JSON 转换为合法的 JavaScript 字符串。

处理来自 Webhook 和 API 的转义 JSON

很多 API 返回的 JSON 中，某些字段包含转义的 JSON 字符串。例如，Webhook 请求体中可能有一个 payload 字段，其值是编码为字符串的 JSON 对象。要读取实际数据，需要先反转义。这在 Stripe Webhook、Slack API 响应和事件驱动架构中很常见。

配置文件中的 JSON

配置文件（package.json、tsconfig.json、.eslintrc）是 JSON 格式，但有时包含特殊字符 — Windows 的反斜杠文件路径、正则表达式或多行描述。正确转义确保这些配置文件保持有效的 JSON 格式。

JSON 转义的常见错误

双重转义

最常见的错误是对已经转义的字符串再次转义。例如，对 She said \"hello\" 再次转义，会得到 She said \\\"hello\\\" — 反斜杠本身被转义，产生错误输出。如果输出有太多反斜杠，很可能就是双重转义了。先用反转义按钮还原，再只转义一次。

忘记转义反斜杠

反斜杠必须先于其他字符被转义。Windows 文件路径 C:\Users\test 在 JSON 中必须写成 C:\\Users\\test。常见错误是转义了引号但忘记转义反斜杠，产生看起来几乎正确但实际损坏的 JSON。

使用错误的转义序列

JSON 只支持有限的转义序列：\"、\\、\/、\n、\r、\t、\b、\f 和 \uXXXX。\a、\v、\0 在 JSON 中无效（虽然在某些编程语言中有效），使用无效序列会导致 JSON.parse 报错。

混合转义和未转义内容

如果粘贴的内容部分转义了（有些引号转义了，有些没有），转义或反转义操作会产生不一致的结果。操作前先确认输入是完全转义还是完全未转义的，然后选择对应的操作。

如何使用 JSON 转义工具

  1. 将 JSON 字符串或文本粘贴到输入框（或上传文件 / 从 URL 加载）
  2. 点击转义添加转义字符，或点击反转义移除转义字符
  3. 复制结果或下载为文件
  4. 使用交换将输出移回输入框进行反向操作

所有处理在浏览器中完成 — 数据不会发送到任何服务器。
